decisions_where_the_design_was_silent: PICK versus authorities: the B4 acceptance says authorities never appear in any model's options, so PICK is used only for questions that are not authorities (MEANING, WHICH_GOAL, UNSETTLED). On a revision, tolerance, counting, convention, source, sheet-complete, always-asks, rule-reading, should-I or legal/medical question, a typed answer is placed by the fixed rules or gets 'please choose one of these'. It never goes to the model. In the design's 2.2 example ('the new one', 'the first', 'Rev A' on the revision question) all three are placed by rules.

'show the limits' gives a revision ASK with no model, which needed a small change to the 0.8.6 dictionary (reading._desk). Before it, the pattern's ambiguity was widened into three MEANING options (select, trace, side by side), each with the revision still open. Without a model that would have needed two cards. The verb is settled by her own pattern, so the only thing open is the revision, and 0.8.6's own rule makes that an ASK.

Legal or medical detection uses reading.CLAIM (sue, claim, court, tribunal) and reading.MEDICAL on the choices and the request. Such a question counts as an authority. RULE_READING, SHOULD_I and OWN_ACCOUNT premises count as authorities too.

Leave it, the 'read default': all choices when every choice is a read and there are at most 3 (judgment's covering-reads rung); otherwise the first choice when it is a read and no authority is open; otherwise CANNOT_TELL with a because sentence for the premise. A navigation is never taken on Leave it.

Buttons: ranked choices, then Something else (a typed-answer field on the same card), then Leave it, for every question. For the old 0.8.6 no-model GOAL buttons, Leave it replaces 'None of these' with the same effect: nothing moves. brief.buttons() and the GOAL fallback are unchanged.

Her ranked order for revisions: the one marked CURRENT first, ARCHIVED last, then the newer revision first. Other choices keep the dictionary's or brief's order. For judgment OWNER questions the gate's own order is kept, because options there carry no revision marks.

of_brief expands an option whose revision stayed open into one choice per revision only when the whole card still fits in 4 choices. Otherwise a click on such an option says cannot tell, and never shows a second card.

A PICK-placed answer carries basis model_pick, so her hand starts it with origin HER: a change on it is never hers at any dial (B1), and reads and navigation are unaffected. A rule-placed typed answer is owner_words and a click is owner_click; only these two offer to keep the phrase (0.8.6 _offer_keep). Rows from agreement are B5's.

PICK caps come from brain_clock.caps('PICK') (new tokens at most 300, answer 4, deadline 6 s). In the smoke the FakeWorker was primed with the PICK brief (messages 1 to 3), as A2's priming does for the live worker, so the cold brief is not counted as new tokens.
